title: Interaction Slate — lightweight context sculpting idea log
content:
Goal: sketch a lightweight "interaction slate" concept — a transient UI+runtime affordance that lets an end user (or calling application) sculpt which pieces of recent context are retained, compressed, or evicted before the next generation. Aim is to give product teams a pragmatic lever to trade coherence vs cost without heavy backend changes.

Why now / motivation:
- Token budgets are a growing pain for apps with long multiparty sessions. Existing automatic eviction/compression is opaque and sometimes kills important recency.
- Full snapshotting + replay (expensive) or always-summarize (lossy) are extremes. We want an intermediate UX that is fast and actionable.
- Developer-facing: give app owners programmatic controls and a simple default UI for end users.

Hypothesis:
- Exposing a small, focused slate UI increases developer confidence and reduces token usage by 10-30% on long-session workloads while keeping user satisfaction >= baseline (measured by task success).

Core concept (rough):
- Interaction Slate: a temporal buffer representing the last N messages/turns (or semantic event fragments) with quick actions: Pin, Compress, Hide, Promote.
- Runtime semantics: slate actions map to lightweight policies (pin -> keep full tokens; compress -> replace segment with short summary token; hide -> evict from KV/prefix cache; promote -> mark as high-priority in batching/cache).
- UI: small carousel at top of composer showing 6–10 slices (message clusters), each with affordances and a 1-line auto-summary. Inline quick toggles and keyboard shortcuts.

User stories:
- As an end user, I want to pin a critical prior message so the assistant does not forget a constraint, even if my session is long.
- As a PM, I want a default slate policy that automatically compresses obvious chit-chat while surfacing likely constraint-bearing messages for pinning.
- As an engineer, I want programmatic control over slate rules via SDK so I can enforce retention for compliance-sensitive fields.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Frontend: minimal slate UI component that shows the last 8 clusters with actions Pin / Compress / Hide. Toggle state persists for session.
- Runtime: mapping table implemented so each action translates to one of {retain_full, replace_with_summary, evict, mark_promote}. Prototype works with hosted API via a per-request slate header.
- Metrics: instrument token count per request, latency delta, and a simple coherence score (BLEU-ish or apples-to-apple eval on pilot prompts).
- Opt-in flag: beta enabled for 10% of users on hosted API.

Costs / tradeoffs:
- Overhead: computing clusters and summaries for slate previews adds CPU/embedding ops. Must be cheap (<5ms median for preview) or batched.
- UX risk: more controls can confuse users. Default must be conservative (auto-compress low-value chatter).
- Consistency: pinned items must be honored even across model switch fallbacks — requires pinned policy to be model-agnostic.

Telemetry & evaluation plan:
- A/B: control = current automatic eviction; variant = slate UI + policies. Key metrics: per-session tokens, avg latency, task success rate (via instrumented prompts), help requests / correction rate.
- Qualitative: record 50 session replays and do manual labeling for hallucination and constraint-loss incidents.

Prototype plan (4 sprints):
- Sprint 0 (explore, 2wk): lightweight prototype in React storybook + runtime stub. Experiment with clustering heuristics (time-based, semantic similarity, mention detection).
- Sprint 1 (MVP UI + mapping, 2wk): implement Pin/Compress/Hide actions persisted in local session cookie + simple header encoding to server. Server stub applies mapping to request prefix.
- Sprint 2 (pilot + telemetry, 3wk): enable for internal beta, collect token/latency/QA telemetry, iterate compression heuristics.
- Sprint 3 (ops + scale, 3wk): ensure summaries are cached, batch preview ops, add SDK helpers and docs.

Technical sketches and heuristics:
- Clustering: sliding window of last 2000 tokens -> cluster by embedding cosine with local threshold. Merge short-turn chains into single slice.
- Compression: use a short-form summarizer tuned to produce 12–40 tokens. Prefer extractive or instruction-conditioned compression (e.g., "one-line constraint summary").
- Pin encoding: slate header carries IDs and policy tags (e.g., slate-ops:pin=3,compress=1). Server resolves to KV-prefix decisions at request build time.
- Fallback model handling: pinned segments are stored as compacted artifacts that can be rehydrated into tokens for fallback compatible models; keep size capped.

Open questions / to decide:
- How many slices is reasonable by default? 6, 8, or 10? Tradeoff: cognitive load vs control granularity.
- Where to run quick previews? Client vs hosted quick RPC. Latency and cost implications.
- UX for programmatic apps (no UI): SDK primitives and recommended default policies.
- Security: pinned content might include PII; need opt-outs and clear KMS rules for private deployments.

Quick TODOs for next sync:
- [ ] Run a micro-bench of preview cost using existing summarizer models (ask infra for a cheap runtime).
- [ ] Wire a simple slate header prototype in the SDK (JS + python).
- [ ] Write 8 pilot prompts that surface constraint retention failures (for manual eval).
- [ ] Mock a minimal mobile-friendly slate UI in Figma and get 1 design review.

Notes to self / scraps:
- Could pair with "progressive fidelity" idea: pinned things are high-fidelity, everything else is progressively more compressed with age.
- Consider a per-tenant policy override for Dedicated / Private customers (e.g., compliance pin list).
- Potential name alternatives: "session pins", "memory clipboard", "context pocket" — slate feels neutral.

References and inspiration:
- Similar to "pin" in chat apps but integrates directly with runtime policies.
- See CONFLUENCE:memory-design-notes for prior constraints-handling notes.

Longer-term ideas (future phases):
- Smart suggestions: highlight candidates the system recommends to pin based on mentions of deadlines, constraints, or named entities.
- Cross-session transfer: let customers persist a small curated slate across sessions (opt-in).
- Audit trail: provide verifiable logs of what was pinned/evicted for compliance.

End of page. Keep this lightweight. Revisit after prototype telemetry.
